Q: WordPress: How can I add categories and tags on pages? A:

This plugin sorted me out:

add-tags-and-category-to-page

with the standard instructions:

Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory Activate the plugin through the 'Plugins' menu in WordPress Use the setting page of the plugin from Settings > Add Tags And Category For Page.

Q: Add Cell and Row in openXML A:

I had the same issue that you had and this article How to: Insert text into a cell in a spreadsheet document (Open XML SDK).

I guess you need to insert a new Cell object into your worksheet and then insert the specified data (assuming it is a string or that it has already being cast into a string) into that cell.

Q: Is coding going to be obsolete? A:

True. But even in different contexts (professional or business), the choice of tools or technologies is still based on scope and preference. I think there will always be at least a niche for hand coding.

Q: How should offensive or hate-related imagery surfaced in reCAPTCHA challenges be reported? A:
  1. Is there an official process for reporting specific reCAPTCHA images that contain offensive or hate-related symbols?

You can (apparently) click the flag icon located in the bottom-left corner of the reCAPTCHA image grid. This opens a form to submit feedback to Google reCAPTCHA.

  1. Does Google review or curate these image datasets when potentially offensive content is identified?

Possibly. More likely they would just delete the offending images.

Only Google can describe their processes for creating the datasets in the first place, and for dealing with this kind of problem. And I doubt they would do that ... unless their hand was forced.

My guess is that AI is involved. Judging from what you saw.

FWIW, there are good reasons (technical, business, legal) for Google not publishing the details of those processes.

  1. Is this considered expected behavior if the symbol happens to appear in a real-world photo that was selected for a challenge category?

Considered by who? Expected by who?

Clearly it is not desirable to show offensive symbols (etcetera) in reCAPTCHA images, and I'm sure that Google didn't do that intentionally ... but if you've seen this once, you shouldn't be totally surprised if you saw it again.

  1. Are there any mechanisms available to website owners or end users to flag problematic challenge images for review?

See answer to 1. And I imagine you (e.g. as a paying Google Cloud Services customer) could submit a support request via https://cloud.google.com/support-hub.
